connections.edgeLabel: Academic base of UAPx's science leadership - NOT a host, sponsor or funder
connections.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
connections.note: The distinction matters and is drawn by the University itself. UAlbany's release separates 'UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy' from 'Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization'. UAPx is an independent 501(c)(3); the University is where its two lead scientists hold their chairs, not its institutional home. This is the opposite of the harvard-cfa / galileo-project relationship already on the board, where the CfA is the host institution. Funding for the 2021 California field work came from Caroline Cory of OMnium Media, to produce the documentary 'A Tear in the Sky' (2022) - not from UAlbany.

desc: UAPx is a small research organisation built by working experimental physicists to do the one thing the field has almost never done: go into the field with calibrated multi-band instrumentation, record everything including the negatives, and publish the protocol. Matthew Szydagis, a liquid-xenon dark-matter physicist at the University at Albany, and Kevin Knuth, a former NASA Ames scientist and Entropy editor, conducted the first UAPx expedition off Catalina Island, California, and published 'Initial results from the first field expedition of UAPx to study unidentified anomalous phenomena' in Progress in Aerospace Sciences volume 156, article 101099, in June 2025, with Benjamin Kugielsky and Cecilia Levy. The paper's value lies in its transparency about instrumentation limits, background rates and false positives - the discipline that comes from a career in an experiment whose principal output is upper limits. In June 2026 Szydagis was named to the UAP Science Advisory Council in the instrumentation and data-collection role, which means the government's outside science body drew its detector expertise from a self-funded civil expedition group rather than from a national laboratory.
